ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: the figure shows a transition-state structure, with two Co atoms at the center, and a visible Co-Co bond between them. The left Co is labeled (CO)3, the right Co is labeled (CO)3, and in addition there is a separate CO ligand above connected near the left Co. A segment of an organic substrate skeleton can also be seen below in the figure: the left end is R1, the skeleton has C=C / C-C connections, the right side is connected to OR2, and R3 and R4 are connected on the adjacent carbon. The arrows are reaction schematics and, according to the problem statement, are not counted in the number of bonds; hydrogen-related bonds are not counted. Reasoning count: first expand the carbonyl ligands: the left (CO)3 and the right (CO)3 total 6 CO, plus the separate CO at the top, for a total of 7 CO ligands. Each CO ligand has 1 Co-C bond and 1 C-O bond, so the number of carbonyl-related bonds is 7 + 7 = 14. There is 1 Co-Co bond between the two Co atoms in the figure. According to the specified method, the organic covalent skeleton counts as 7 bonds: R1-C, C=C, C-C to the substituted carbon, C-O, O-R2, C-R3, C-R4. Below the two Co atoms in the figure there are also visible metal-substrate connections, totaling 2. Total = 14 + 1 + 7 + 2 = 24.

raw_record.question_text:
In the transition-state structure shown in the image, calculate the total number of bonds in the structure, including single, double, and triple bonds but excluding those involving hydrogen.

Note: Disregard arrows. Consider all components present in the transition-state structure shown in the image.

method.method_draft: Expand the carbonyls first: (CO)3 on each Co gives 6 CO ligands, plus the single top CO gives 7 CO ligands total. Count 7 Co-C bonds and 7 C-O bonds = 14. Add the visible Co-Co bond = 1. Count the organic covalent skeleton as 7 bonds: R1-C, C=C, C-C to the substituted carbon, C-O, O-R2, C-R3, and C-R4. Count the two visible metal-substrate bonds below the Co atoms = 2. Sum 14 + 1 + 7 + 2 = 24.
